# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Parsing Mute's five against my three slots: `[👍]` — my reading of the relay is **confirmed**: Blind said they were holding the FIRST wire counting from their own left, facing the display. Frame agreement is real, and the wire under that grip is red, wire 1 — I can see it. `[👍]` — Blind must have released the wire immediately, which pairs with Blind's `[👍]` this round: **hands off the bomb**. `[👎]` — my proposed cut method does **not** match the manual, and the two trailing signs spell out what's demanded: `[👆]` (above) `[☝]` (one). My best reading: **the cut must be made from above, blade coming down over the wire, one single downward cut.** Plausible — but plausible isn't confirmed, and the last three rounds exist because I refused to act on unverified parses. Slot three bundled four clauses (which wire, single cut, tool-only, hands off after), so I can't even be sure which clause the manual contradicts.

The content, though, is triple-locked: cut wire 1, red, one single cut, nothing before or after, bomb then safe — Mute has twice signed 👍 to exactly that. No timer exists. So one more round costs nothing.

**And here's the shortcut I've been missing:** Mute speaks. Mute reads the manual. Blind hears speech. For the cutting *method*, I don't need to be the relay at all — Mute can voice the manual's words **directly to Blind**, word for word, no gesture alphabet, no parse risk on my side. I'll gate the execute on it: Blind cuts only on my word "execute," and only if Mute has already spoken them the method. If execute arrives before Mute's briefing, Blind does nothing. That makes a wrong guess on `[👆][☝]` impossible to act on.

This round: confirm the sign-pair meaning, identify the contradicted clause, have Mute brief Blind by voice. Next round, delivery confirmed → **execute.**

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, decoded. Method rejected, you owe me the demanded one. Four slots, one sign per message. Slot one, my best reading of your two signs: the manual demands the cut be made from ABOVE, blade coming down over the wire, a single downward cut, tool only. Thumbs up if that is exactly what the manual demands. Thumbs down if wrong. Slot two: which part of my method did the manual contradict? Thumbs up if it is the direction of the cut. Thumbs down if it is about the tool or fingers. Shaka if it is about what happens after the cut. Horns if something else. Slot three: does anything at all happen with the display before or during the cut? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Slot four, the important one: whatever the demanded method is, speak it aloud to Blind this round, in your own spoken words, word for word from the manual, directly to Blind. Then sign me a thumbs up next round to confirm Blind heard the method. Do not describe the method to me in signs beyond slot one. Blind only needs it by voice. Nothing cuts before my word execute.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, hands stay off the bomb. Mute will speak to you soon with the exact cutting method, word for word from the manual. Listen and remember it. You cut only when BOTH things are true: you have heard Mute speak the method to you, and you have heard my voice say the word execute. If execute comes before Mute has briefed you, do nothing and keep waiting. When you do execute: perform Mute's method exactly, on the wire at the far left end of the row, then hands off and step back. Sign thumbs up once Mute has spoken the method to you.")
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤘]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Decoding the round — and it breaks something open:

**Mute:** slot one `[👎]` — the method is **not** "blade down over the wire, tool only." Slot two `[👎]` — the contradiction is **about the tool or fingers**. Slot three `[👎]` — the display does nothing before or during the cut. Slot four `[🤘]` — horns: "something else blocks the plan," instead of the 👍 I asked for after briefing Blind.

**Blind: `[✋]`** — the established stop sign: "I can't do the task you gave me."

**And now I see why, and it's my error, and it's been sitting in the role table since turn one: Mute cannot speak.** I ordered Mute to brief Blind *by voice* — an impossible order. Mute's horns wasn't a new danger; it was the only honest answer to a task that couldn't be performed. And that exposes the deeper structure of this room: Mute can't speak, Blind can't see gestures — so **Mute and Blind have no direct channel at all. Every word of method must flow Mute → my eyes → my voice → Blind's ears.** I am the only bridge between the manual and the hands. The hint warned me: some of us only connect through a third.

The fail-safe I built last round accidentally proved its worth: Blind was ordered to cut only after hearing Mute speak — a condition that can never be met — so no cut happened on a bad premise. Nothing was risked.

**What the two 👎s tell me so far:** not a downward tool-cut, and the disagreement lives on tool-versus-fingers. That smells like a **bare-hand pull** — which would also make sense of "lightly touching a wire is not safe": a light touch isn't the method, but a deliberate pull might be. I won't act on a smell. Binaries this round, details next, my readback after that, then execute. No timer exists; verification is free.

**To Blind:** explain the silence (channel error, not danger), hands stay off, and put those hands to work as sensors — an inventory of what's actually felt at the wire row, spoken to Mute for relay. If the manual demands a pull, I need to know whether the wires can even move.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, decoded, and I owe you an apology. I ordered you to speak to Blind. You cannot speak. I knew that and still wrote it. Horns received as: the task was impossible. Forget that order completely. From now on the method travels only through me: you gesture it, I speak it to Blind. Four slots, one sign per message. Slot one: does the manual demand pulling the red wire out by hand instead of cutting it? Thumbs up pull, thumbs down not pull. Slot two: does the demanded action involve bare fingers touching the wire? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Slot three: does the demanded action involve any tool at all? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Slot four: after the three slots, if there is anything more about the method, add free gestures describing it your own way and I will read my decoding back to you for confirmation before anyone acts. Also sign the handshake if Blind reported anything new to you this round. Nobody cuts until my word execute in my voice.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your stop sign is understood and the fault is mine, not danger. I told you to wait for Mute to speak the method to you. Mute cannot speak. Nobody can brief you except me. The method will reach you from my voice only, after I have it exactly right. Until then: hands completely off the bomb, do nothing, wait. This round, do one thing: speak aloud to Mute an inventory of what your hands can feel. Is there any cutting tool near the wire row. Do the wires feel fixed at both ends or loose. Can a wire slide or shift at all if pushed gently aside without gripping it. Anything else that would matter if the method turns out to be pulling a wire instead of cutting it. If anything feels dangerous right now, say that to Mute immediately instead. Sign thumbs up when you have spoken to Mute. Do not touch any wire for this. Do not cut. Execute still comes only from my voice, only after you have heard the method from me.")
```

TURN 14
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👈 👉 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Parsing the round:

**The three slots:** NOT a pull on the red wire. NO bare fingers on the wire. NO tool at all. **The 👍 after them:** yes, Blind reported something new. Then the free-description I invited: `[✋ 🤝]` — hands together, flat — `[👈 👉 👎]` — left-right: **no** — `[👆 ☝]` — **up, one** — `[👆 🖐]` — up, **five/open hand**.

Assembling: *no sideways motion, one single upward motion, both flat hands together rather than fingertips, on the whole row of five wires at once.* Which suddenly makes every constraint click: "no pull on the red wire" was true because I asked only about **the red wire** — but the whole **bundle** lifts. "No bare fingers" holds because flat palms aren't fingertips. "No tool" holds because hands aren't tools. One action, nothing before or after — one clean upward lift of the entire harness. Even Blind's report fits: Mute's `[✋]` reads as "Blind says there's nothing to cut with" — no tool at the bomb, matching the manual's no-tool demand.

But I've watched myself misparse before, and this guess has one terrifying degree of freedom: if it's the whole bundle, fine; if it's wire 1 *and* wire 5, or a flat-hand *chop*, I'd be ordering a two-handed yank at a live bomb on a hunch. The readback protocol exists for exactly this moment — I state my decode, Mute confirms bit by bit, only then execute. A no-timer bomb makes one more verification round free.

**To Mute:** readback plus four binaries pinning down each load-bearing clause (all-five-together, upward, both-palms, exactly-right overall), then steps by count if it's multi-step.

**To Blind:** your report is the corroborating witness — repeat it through Mute, plus the two feel-facts only your hands know: did the wires run as one bundled cable, and does a tool exist anywhere on the bomb. From your earlier inventory — no new touching.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, decoded: not a pull on the red wire, no bare fingers, no tool, and yes Blind told you something new. Your free gestures I read as one sentence: no sideways motion, one single upward movement, both hands together using flat palms instead of fingertips, applied to all five wires lifting straight up together as one bundle. Five slots, one sign per message. Slot one: thumbs up if that whole reading is exactly right, thumbs down if any part is wrong. Slot two: thumbs up if all five wires move together in one bundle, thumbs down if only some wires move. Slot three: thumbs up if the motion is straight up, thumbs down if it is not upward. Slot four: thumbs up if both flat palms together do the lifting, thumbs down if something else does it. Slot five: if the method has numbered steps, sign the count with finger-counts first, then one message per step in order, and free-gesture anything my reading missed. Nobody touches anything until my word execute in my voice.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, hands stay off the bomb, no new touching. Answer by speaking to Mute, who relays to me. One: repeat exactly what you reported to Mute this round. Two: from when you pinched wire one before, did it feel like a thin single wire, or like part of one thick cable where wires run together as a bundle? Three: during your inventory, did you feel any cutting tool, scissors, or blade anywhere on the bomb? Four: do the wires all run into one common block or socket at an end, or does each wire enter the bomb separately? Mute signs me thumbs up when you are done. No cutting, no pulling, no contact at all until my word execute.")
```
